title: NextLevel Pulsar brewing guide
scope: Full-size NextLevel Pulsar with a compatible paper filter, using the 20 g example of Jonathan Gagne's published steeped-bloom percolation recipe; everyday app defaults, metal discs and Mini procedures are separately identified.

sources.title: Pulsar User Guide
supports: Paper assembly and rinse
Horizontal closed valve and recommended 12-to-3-o'clock travel
General closed-start 3x bloom lasting 30-60 seconds
Low water level and normal slowing near the end
Base-only lifting, cleaning and disassembled storage
General 15-40 g dosing and 4-7 minute range; these are not the chosen creator recipe's exact targets

sources.title: NextLevel Pulsar Brewer
supports: 380 mL chamber liquid volume
Manufacturer-selected 20 g / 340 g batch
Flow valve, dispersion cap and no-bypass design

sources.title: The Pulsar Dripper
supports: 20-30 g recipe with relatively coarse grind
Wet-base paper priming to minimize trapped air
Open-start 3x bloom, close at first dripping, gentle agitation
99 C for the author's light roasts
Release at 60 seconds and small pulses maintaining roughly 1 cm above the bed
1:17 total input ratio and 210-270 second target

sources.title: NextLevel Pulsar Recipes and Recommendations
supports: 25 g dose, 17:1 input water ratio, 75 g bloom and water just off the boil
45-60 second recipe-outline bloom; detailed release sequence begins around 45-50 seconds
1-2 cm water level, short bursts and final gentle swirl
Firm barrel assembly with threaded end downward
Personal 20 g minimum recommendation, rather than a hardware limit

sources.title: NextLevel Pulsar Dripper Brew Recipe
supports: Closed-start 20 g paper recipe with 60 mL bloom and 320 mL total
Upright open and horizontal closed valve
Published ZP6 5-6 and Fellow Ode Gen 2 printed 5.2 suggestions in that recipe's context
One-minute release, 100 mL first post-bloom pour then roughly 40 mL pulses
Recipe mixes volume wording with dose-weight multiples; no exact mass conversion is claimed here

Current product detail lists 2 x 40k
Metal may tolerate less agitation before clogging than paper
Dump grounds with barrel inserted, then disassemble and carefully remove disc with valve open
Wash after each use and protect thin discs in storage case

Exact 19K/40K hole-count specification and comparative clarity ranking remain unverified
Customer reviews mentioning 19k are not manufacturer specifications

sources.title: NextLevel Pulsar Mini Recipes
supports: Mini adaption requires reconsidering dose, bed depth, grind and agitation
Mini wet-base paper priming is less successful; dry-filter start suggested

sources.title: Brewing Suggestions
supports: General 94 C and 1:17 starting suggestions provide context for the app's everyday default
General suggestions do not establish an exact 45-second, five-pulse recipe or universal decaf finish target

recipe.name: Jonathan Gagne steeped bloom, 20 g / 340 g paper example
equipment: Full-size NextLevel Pulsar with base, barrel and dispersion cap
Stable heat-safe server that supports the brewer level and holds the collected brew
recipe.grind_description: Relatively coarse and even, a little coarser than a typical 20 g V60 grind; tune on this brewer without inferring a grinder dial value or precise micron conversion.

expected_time_s.clock_start: Start the timer as the first 60 g bloom pour begins
expected_time_s.clock_end: Final drawdown: standing water has gone and flow has subsided to final drips

recipe.completion_signal: No standing water above the coffee bed and the final drawdown has subsided; close the valve and lift only by the base. The time range is a comparison target, not forced completion.

steps.instruction: With the barrel off, close the valve, add a shallow water layer just above the ridges, place dry paper on it, open over the sink, and close again. Fit the barrel firmly, threaded end downward.
steps.why: Seat the filter with minimal trapped air. This rinse is discarded and excluded from the brew input.
steps.completion: Paper flat on ridges; barrel firmly seated with no leak. Valve closed.

steps.instruction: Place level on a stable server and scale, add 20 g coffee, level gently without tamping, fit the cap and tare. Stabilize the base while operating the valve: horizontal is closed, upright is open.
steps.why: A level coffee bed and supported brewer allow even wetting and safe valve operation.
steps.completion: Level coffee bed, cap fitted and scale reads zero.

steps.instruction: Open the valve, start the timer and pour 60 g through the dispersion cap. Close as soon as dripping begins, even during the pour, and finish reaching 60 g. Holding only the base, swirl gently to wet dry pockets.
steps.why: The brief open start displaces air between coffee particles; closing then retains the bloom. Avoid driving fines into the paper with strong agitation.
steps.completion: Scale at 60 g, grounds wet, valve closed and bloom retained.

steps.instruction: Keep the valve closed until elapsed time reaches 60 seconds from the beginning of the first pour.
steps.why: Allow saturation before draining resumes; 60 seconds is an elapsed release point, not an extra wait after pouring.
steps.completion: Elapsed timer reads 60 seconds; retained bloom remains wet.

steps.instruction: At elapsed 60 seconds open the valve fully. Add 280 g through the cap in small pulses, keeping about 1 cm of water over the bed; stop at 340 g cumulative. With a gooseneck kettle, Gagne recommends relatively fast circular pouring to avoid digging holes; ordinary kettles also work. No fixed pulse count, size or universal pouring rate is specified.
steps.why: The low pool supports ongoing percolation while limiting unnecessarily tall water levels. The total already includes the 60 g bloom.
steps.completion: 340 g cumulative brew water has entered; level safely below rim.

steps.instruction: Let final drawdown finish with the valve open. Once standing water is gone and flow subsides, close, lift only by the base, set down safely, and serve.
steps.why: Slowing as the water level drops is normal; drainage rather than a timer deadline determines removal.
steps.completion: Final drawdown complete; brewer safely removed by the base.

variants.name: App everyday default
variants.how_it_differs: App-authored combination: 1:17, 3x closed-start bloom for 45 seconds, 93-96 C, five equal post-bloom pulses and 210-270 second reference. At a chosen 20 g dose this is 60 g bloom plus five 56 g pulses. No creator source establishes that entire combination. General manufacturer suggestions support a roughly 94 C start and 30-60 second blooms. Do not relabel it Gagne.

variants.name: Scott Rao's 25 g example
variants.how_it_differs: 25 g coffee and 425 g total input at 1:17, 75 g bloom, just-off-boil water, recipe-outline 45-60 second bloom, approximately 1-2 cm water level and final gentle swirl. In the detailed sequence he adds water around 45-50 seconds before opening. This is not the 20 g / 340 g Gagne workflow.

variants.name: Kaldi's 20 g paper recipe
variants.how_it_differs: 20 g dose, closed-start bloom stated as 60 mL or 3x dose, release at 60 seconds, then 100 mL and roughly 40 mL pulses to 320 mL total. Published ZP6 5-6 and Ode Gen 2 printed 5.2 suggestions belong to this recipe and filter. Source mixes grams and milliliters; an exact 320 g mass recipe is not asserted.

variants.name: Metal disc
variants.how_it_differs: Reusable filtration with separate agitation and care behavior. Manufacturer warns it may clog with less agitation than paper. Retain and protect the disc; dump grounds while barrel remains fitted, then disassemble. No exact dose, temperature, pulse schedule or comparative 19K/40K clarity recipe verified; specification evidence remains partial.

variants.name: Pulsar Mini
variants.how_it_differs: Smaller filter and different bed depth require recipe reassessment. Manufacturer favors a dry-filter start because floating paper on a wet base works less well; do not reuse the full-size priming procedure automatically.

variants.name: Steep-and-release
variants.how_it_differs: Manufacturer also permits retaining all recipe water, stirring, steeping then releasing. This uses a different grind/contact-time model and must fit the chamber with coffee and headroom; no exact beginner recipe is invented here.

troubleshooting.symptom: Little flow or a stalled drawdown
troubleshooting.check_first: Ensure valve is fully open, filter flat, barrel correctly assembled, brewer level and cap clean. Distinguish normal gradual slowing at a low water level from a stall.
troubleshooting.adjustment: For the next brew reduce agitation; if it still stalls, try a coarser grind. The manufacturer's water-first bloom is a separate experiment, not an automatic alteration of the named recipe.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm dose, 340 g cumulative input including bloom, temperature and wetting; verify no assembly leak bypassed the grounds.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Try a slightly finer grind with otherwise unchanged procedure. Taste remains the deciding evidence.

troubleshooting.symptom: Drying harshness or bitter roast character
troubleshooting.check_first: Check for excessive agitation, very fine grind and a tall water pool; identify whether the roast is more developed than the chosen light-roast example.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Try coarser or less agitation. For a more developed roast, separately test cooler water. Do not add a universal grinder-click count.

troubleshooting.check_first: After cooling and cleaning, inspect correct insertion and damaged parts. Do not fight a stiff valve while an unsupported hot brewer can tip.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Follow manufacturer maintenance instructions for food-safe silicone lubrication and fully inserted valve, or contact manufacturer if damaged or still leaking.

safety: Lift the assembled brewer only by its base whenever it contains hot brew water; never lift it by the barrel walls.
Support the brewer and server level and stabilize the base during valve operation. Stop pouring before approaching the rim; ensure server capacity is sufficient.
Chamber liquid volume is 380 mL; coffee displaces space. It is not a 380 g cumulative-water limit or permission to retain 340 g plus coffee without checking level.

Keep brewer parts off hot surfaces, inspect for damage and wash before first use. Hand washing is encouraged; dishwasher use is allowed but detergent residues can affect taste. Avoid chlorine or bleach.

After cooling, dispose of paper/grounds, rinse and wipe oils from the barrel; store with barrel removed. Metal discs require the separate manufacturer cleanup, washing and protective storage procedure.

app_audit.finding: Current PULSAR defaults: 1:17, 3x bloom, five pulses, 93-96 C, 210-270 seconds and medium-coarse grind; constructor inheritance supplies 45-second bloom, 2.0 g/g apparent loss and standard decaf timing. At an example 20 g dose, BrewCalculator computes 340 g water, 60 g bloom, 280 g remaining and five 56 g pulses, cumulative 60/116/172/228/284/340.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Describe this as an app-authored everyday starting recipe. Keep it distinct from Gagne's 99 C, 60-second release and water-level-controlled pulses; retain input-water accounting.

app_audit.finding: Current shared completion: 'When drawdown is complete, remove the brewer carefully and serve the coffee.' Shared warning at line 311: 'Hot water and brewed coffee can burn. Keep hands clear of the hot liquid and use a stable surface.' Neither gives manufacturer base-only lifting. The separate Learn resource's stage 8 already does.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Add lift-only-by-base to always-visible shared safety and completion, including handling during agitation. Preserve the correct Learn warning.

app_audit.finding: Current BrewMethod.kt:98 is 'capacityMaxG = 380'. BrewCalculator lines 74-75 calculate 'if (method.capacityMaxG != null && waterG > method.capacityMaxG)' then 'kotlin.math.ceil(waterG.toDouble() / method.capacityMaxG).toInt() - 1'. This divides cumulative input mass by a chamber liquid-volume specification of 380 mL. Draining percolation can use more cumulative water than instantaneous chamber capacity and coffee occupies space.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Model volume/headroom separately from cumulative recipe water. Use low-water-level and overflow cues; do not describe total input exceeding 380 g as a required reservoir refill.

app_audit.finding: Pulsar prediction uses 2.2 g apparent loss per g coffee with PROTOCOL_SENSITIVE caveat; BrewMethod.kt:79/BrewCalculator.kt:41 fall back to 2.0. For 20/340 these predict 296 g and 300 g respectively without personal calibration. No reviewed source establishes either as universal or a fixed beverage target.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve estimated-output wording, consolidate estimation semantics where displayed, and use measured calibration when available. Do not place a predicted yield in the exact creator recipe as a verified target.

app_audit.finding: Pulsar inherits STANDARD decaf policy, subtracting 30 seconds from both target bounds via BrewCalculator.kt:63, making 180-240 seconds. The reviewed Pulsar creator/manufacturer sources do not establish a universal decaf timing shortcut.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Remove unsupported automatic time subtraction or clearly label it an unvalidated app heuristic; tune by observed drainage and taste. Do not silently modify a named fixed recipe for decaf.

app_audit.finding: Roast-date rule makes Pulsar bloom 55 s at <=7 days, 45 s through 21 days, and 35 s thereafter. Prep/timer use effectiveBloomDurationSeconds, but LegacyBrewSessionStartFactory.kt:124 passes the static 45 s for Pulsar, and LegacyStagePlanFactory.kt:29,140 compiles it. Exact age thresholds and offsets are not supported by reviewed sources.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Resolve timing consistency between displayed and durable recipes. Keep named Gagne 60-second release intact and classify any freshness adaptation as separately reviewed app behavior rather than a source requirement.

app_audit.finding: Learn correctly contains paper priming, 20/340 at 1:17, 60 g open-start bloom, first-drip closure, 99 C, release at 60 s, remaining 280 g, low pool and observable drawdown with base-only lifting. Stage 3 completion says both 60 g and first drops, before stage 4 closes; this can imply waiting for 60 g despite earlier dripping. It explains initial open bloom as displacing air below paper rather than Gagne's between-particle air. Central pouring tip differs from his gooseneck circular-pattern advice.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Keep existing quantities. Merge or clarify the closure cue during the bloom pour, revise air explanation, and describe steady circular pouring through the cap for a gooseneck kettle while retaining ordinary-kettle support. This is a minor procedural clarification, not an unresolved wholesale recipe contradiction.

app_audit.finding: PulsarLearnGuideCatalog is a standalone timer-free educational guide, intentionally outside exact-session P1 recipe contracts. BuiltInP1RecipeCatalog and P1ExactGuidanceFactualErrata contain no Pulsar recipe/erratum. Numeric target extraction in all 23 raw*/pulsar_learn_guidance.json locale files matched 20/340, 60, 99, 60-second release, 280 remaining, 1 cm, 210-270 second target and eight stages.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Do not claim P1 catalog presence, full everyday support or approved translation from the existence of this Learn guide. Translation semantics, images, accessibility speech and device behavior require their own review.

app_audit.finding: Comment explicitly excludes claims about 19K/40K behavior, but content applies by standard brewer profile and tells users to prepare their selected compatible filter, use a closed bloom and open for remaining water. BrewTimerScreen.kt:680 likewise closes through the entire bloom and opens afterward. This matches the general paper manual but is not an exact Gagne recipe and has no separately verified metal recipe.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Keep general paper-default procedure identified; gate or supplement metal guidance with the selected filter's own care/agitation information. Never present the profile-wide copy as proof of metal timings or as Gagne's open-start technique.

app_audit.finding: METAL_19K description asserts '19,000 holes' and METAL_40K at line 20 asserts '40,000 holes' plus 'cleaner than 19K'. BrewingCatalog.kt:84,91 marks both filter profiles HIGH confidence. Current actual manufacturer page lists 2 x 40k and generic metal body/agitation/care; customer review mentions 19k, but exact counts or comparative filtering performance remain partial evidence.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Retain compatibility identifiers if needed but replace unsupported hole-count/performance assertions with verified medium/care facts and reassess confidence. Do not turn product shorthand or customer testimony into a technical specification.

app_audit.finding: Paper-only ZP6 5-6 band uses app-selected 5.2; Ode Gen 2 entry at line 201 preserves published printed 5.2 as 5 plus two thirds. Asset version 4 explicitly removed metal predictions; DefaultGrinders.kt:40 preserves paper-only ZP6 fallback. Kaldi's source recipe is 20 g / 320 mL rather than Gagne's 20 g / 340 g.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve filter and exact-model boundaries and source notation; identify the source recipe context and app-chosen ZP6 point. Do not infer grinder values for metal, different burrs/calibration, or a different recipe. Keep unsupported combinations generic.

app_audit.finding: Generic Pulsar troubleshooting prescribes 2-4 clicks coarser; line 451 prescribes 3-5 clicks plus rest 7+ days. Click magnitude differs by grinder and reviewed sources provide no universal seven-day rest rule. Line 448's dose >=20 g resembles Rao's personal preference, whereas manufacturer supports 15-40 g.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Check valve/filter/setup first, reduce agitation then use a small grinder-specific or texture-based change. Frame dose changes as recipe-dependent bed-depth choices and fresh-coffee gas as observable behavior; remove universal increments/rest deadlines.

app_audit.finding: Generated Pulsar ratio presets label 1:16 Bright, 1:17 Balanced and 1:18 Rich, although more input water normally reduces concentration for a similar extraction. Flavour cannot be fixed from ratio alone. strings.xml:87 says Most users brew 20-25 g without population evidence.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Use concrete strength labels for ratio choices and describe 20-25 g as a useful starting range, rather than a surveyed majority or guaranteed flavour.

app_audit.finding: Historical audit calls the 60 g bloom closed-valve without restating the brief open start; current Learn resource already contains the open-start step. General user-guide 4-7 minute timing and Gagne's 210-270 s target cover different recipe scopes.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Treat the previous audit as historical evidence. Record this fresh review without rewriting immutable projections or reporting an already-present open-start step as missing.

uncertainties: No physical brew, device execution, release validation or approved localization review was performed.

Metal evidence is partial: the manufacturer's actual care text was verified through the in-app browser after repeated web-fetch timeouts; direct terminal retrieval was blocked by socket permissions. Exact 19K/40K hole-count specifications and comparative clarity were not verified.

Gagne's recipe selects light roasts and 99 C; darker roasts, changed dose, different paper generation, water chemistry, grinder distribution and altitude may change the best starting point and total time.
Rao's outline says 45-60 seconds while the detailed sequence adds water around 45-50 seconds before opening. It is retained as a range rather than rewritten to an exact 60-second release.
Kaldi's published recipe mixes mass multiples and water volumes. Its 320 mL total is not silently converted to exact mass.
No universal beverage-retention coefficient, decaf timing adjustment, roast-age bloom offset or precise grinder conversion was established.
General manufacturer 4-7 minute timing is not a contradiction with the selected creator 210-270 second example; the procedures and batch scopes differ.
do_not_claim: The everyday 45-second, 93-96 C and five-equal-pulse default is Jonathan Gagne's exact published recipe.
The brewer must finish by 270 seconds, regardless of recipe, coffee or taste.
380 mL instantaneous chamber volume is 380 g maximum cumulative brew water, or all 340 g can always be safely retained with the coffee.
340 g input water equals 340 g or 340 mL collected coffee.
Metal 19K and 40K use the paper recipe unchanged, have verified exact hole counts, or a proven clarity ranking.
A grinder micron estimate determines a precise dial value on arbitrary hardware or calibration.
All decaf should finish 30 seconds sooner or all fresh coffee requires a fixed seven-day rest.
An educational Learn guide or numeric parity across locales establishes exact-session support, translated-language accuracy, image accuracy, physical brewing success or release readiness.
